newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast gasolines led higher by Bay run cuts.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast gasolines led higher by Bay run cuts.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot wholesale gasoline prices rose in quiet Wednesday trading on rumors of tightening supply in San Francisco, traders said.

CARB gasoline spot prices, which collapsed from 87 to 60 cents the last six weeks, appeared to stabilize Wednesday, as a major San Francisco refiner admitted cutting the amount of crude it processes starting earlier this week.
Tosco, which has a combined crude distillation capacity of 250,000 barrels-per-day (bpd) in the city, said it cut back intake of crude oil, but declined to say how much.
Other refiners were rumored to be cutting use of crude, which has risen dramatically compared to products.
"I'm hearing rumors that everybody's cutting runs in the Bay," one trader said.
Futures helped push spot values higher, with unleaded gasoline for June delivery ending 1.14 cents a gallon higher at 66.53 cents.
Crude oil rose 27 cents a barrel to $21.86 cents a barrel.
++ GASOLINE: Traders pegged offers for May CARB unleaded gasoline at 62 cents a gallon in Los Angeles, up a half cent from Tuesday.
San Francisco CARB gasoline narrowed its usual two-cent discount to L.A., a higher demand market. May CARB gasoline rose about two cents to stand a half cent under the L.A.

In conventional trade, players said two ship were scheduled to leave San Francisco next week with cargoes of conventional gasoline. The grade remained two cents under its L.A. counterpart, at 57/58 cents, unchanged from Tuesday.

++ DISTILLATES: Trade shifted to June shipments, with offers for CARB diesel in L.A. at 62.50/63.50 cents, flat from Tuesday. Low sulphur diesel, or "EPA" grade edged up 0.50 cents a gallon while jet stood 61./62.
